title: Execution Models Across Languages

weeks.focus: Model and freeze memory, scheduler, type-boundary, workload-equivalence, and failure predictions
Build and verify one bounded fan-out contract in TypeScript, Go, Rust, and Java
Break and measure scheduler, allocation, race, cancellation, resource, and validation failures
Compare runtimes, decide, teach, assess, remediate, and complete Gate 5

readiness_note: Draft until polyglot conformance, paired failure tests, six isolated evaluator runs, calibration checking, semantic review, resource verification, and focused and full-course validation pass.

outcomes.statement: Explain and compare stack, heap, allocation, escape, manual lifetime, RAII, ownership, reference counting, and tracing collection from workload evidence.
Trace work through operating-system threads, event loops, worker pools, goroutines, async tasks, virtual threads, and runtime schedulers.
Implement the same bounded fan-out contract in TypeScript, Go, Rust, and Java with bounded admission, deadlines, cancellation, validation, and cleanup.
Measure latency, useful throughput, queueing, memory, allocation, and garbage collection under equivalent work without treating host noise as a language property.
Diagnose memory-visibility and data-race failures with happens-before reasoning, detector evidence, and explicit detector limits.
Preserve contracts across static, dynamic, process, and serialization boundaries through explicit validation and scoped authority.
Diagnose nine execution-model failures while bounding operational, security, cost, migration, and ownership consequences.
Defend and teach a runtime choice from workload behavior, safety, operability, ecosystem, cost, migration, ownership, and team evidence.

resources.title: Don't Block the Event Loop (or the Worker Pool)
resources.purpose: Trace event-loop and worker-pool placement and connect blocking to tail latency and denial of service.
resources.assignment: Read Should you read this guide through Don't block the Worker Pool; classify each Northstar operation and record one bound per scheduler.

resources.title: The Go Memory Model
resources.purpose: Reason about visibility through happens-before edges.
resources.assignment: Read the introduction, advice, and synchronization sections; draw two valid edges and one behavior the model does not promise.

resources.title: Understanding Ownership
resources.purpose: Connect ownership and borrowing to release timing and safe sharing.
resources.assignment: Read Chapter 4; annotate ownership transfer, borrow lifetime, Drop point, and one resource whose operational release still needs explicit evidence.

resources.title: Virtual Threads
resources.purpose: Distinguish virtual from platform threads and avoid treating cheap tasks as unbounded work.
resources.assignment: Read What Is a Virtual Thread through Guidelines; identify carrier scheduling, blocking concerns, cancellation obligations, and the admission bound still required.

resources.title: Type Compatibility
resources.purpose: Separate structural compile-time compatibility from validation of untrusted runtime values.
resources.assignment: Read Starting Out, A Note on Soundness, function compatibility, and classes; construct one value that type-checks locally but must be rejected after JSON decoding.

resources.title: Why Discord Is Switching from Go to Rust
resources.purpose: Evaluate a workload-specific runtime change without turning an old result into a universal language ranking.
resources.assignment: Read the complete article including version notes; extract workload, measurement, migration, ecosystem, and team evidence, then name three reasons the result cannot be generalized to current toolchains.

resources.title: Queues, Fairness, and the Go Scheduler
resources.author_or_publisher: Madhav Jivrajani; GopherCon and Microsoft Learn
resources.purpose: Build a concrete scheduler model and connect fairness telemetry to runnable work.
resources.assignment: Watch with captions; draw goroutine-to-thread scheduling, record two fairness mechanisms, and identify one claim requiring current runtime verification.

resources.title: Java Language Specification, Chapter 17: Threads and Locks
resources.author_or_publisher: Oracle and the Java Community Process
resources.purpose: Use formal happens-before rules when evaluating visibility and synchronization in Java.
resources.assignment: Read 17.4.2 through 17.4.7; explain program order, synchronization order, volatile edges, and why repeated observations are not evidence of race freedom.

resources.title: Data Race Detector
resources.purpose: Interpret dynamic race evidence without treating an unobserved race as proof of absence.
resources.assignment: Read Introduction, Usage, Typical Data Races, and Runtime Overhead; record the F06 command, one observed conflict, and two coverage limits.

resources.title: Extensible Concurrency with Send and Sync
resources.purpose: Bound what Rust's Send and Sync traits reject and what protocol invariants remain unproved.
resources.assignment: Read the full section; explain the F06 compile-fail fixture and name two runtime or protocol failures static rejection does not exclude.

resources.title: Introduction to Garbage Collection Tuning
resources.purpose: Relate allocation rate, heap pressure, pause evidence, and throughput without inferring a collector result from RSS alone.
resources.assignment: Read the introduction and Factors Affecting Garbage Collection Performance; connect one factor to F05 and record what telemetry would falsify the first explanation.

resources.title: Node.js Releases
resources.purpose: Justify the supported production release line used by the reproducible lab.
resources.assignment: Inspect the release table and policy; record the pinned line, its support state, and the date on which the choice must be revisited.

resources.title: Go Release History
resources.purpose: Verify the exact Go toolchain used by the lab and bound version-specific observations.
resources.assignment: Locate the pinned release notes and record one scheduler, runtime, or tool behavior that must not be generalized to another version.

resources.title: Rust Releases
resources.purpose: Verify the pinned Rust compiler and preserve the version boundary of compile-time evidence.
resources.assignment: Locate the pinned release and record why compiler identity belongs in both successful and compile-fail evidence.

resources.title: Oracle Java SE Support Roadmap
resources.purpose: Separate language/runtime behavior from vendor lifecycle and support decisions.
resources.assignment: Confirm Java 25's lifecycle designation and record one vendor-neutral and one vendor-specific consequence for the ADR.

failure_experiments.scenario: Node event-loop blocking delays unrelated requests
failure_experiments.evidence: request hash, injected CPU work, event-loop delay, journey latency, partition decision, and I03

failure_experiments.scenario: Node or Java worker exhaustion creates an unbounded wait
failure_experiments.evidence: admissions, queue depth, active workers, explicit overload results, and I02

failure_experiments.scenario: Go goroutine or detached task survives request cancellation
failure_experiments.evidence: task identities, cancellation time, cleanup grace, active-task delta, and I04

failure_experiments.scenario: unbounded allocation pressure exceeds the memory budget
failure_experiments.evidence: equivalent bytes, allocation mode, peak memory, admission decision, and I08

failure_experiments.scenario: tracing garbage collection creates an unmeasured latency pause
failure_experiments.evidence: heap limit, allocation rate, GC count and pause, tail latency, Rust contrast boundary, and I09

failure_experiments.scenario: unsynchronized shared state produces a data race
failure_experiments.evidence: conflicting accesses, happens-before graph, detector output, repaired synchronization, Rust compile-fail contrast, and I07

failure_experiments.scenario: downstream work ignores the caller deadline and cancellation
failure_experiments.evidence: parent and child deadlines, cancellation reason, completion time, orphan count, and I03-I04

failure_experiments.scenario: response or file resources remain open after completion
failure_experiments.evidence: acquisition and release identity, open-resource delta, exception path, and I05

failure_experiments.scenario: TypeScript shape assumptions accept invalid JSON at the process boundary
failure_experiments.evidence: wire bytes, compile-time type, validation result, safe rejection, request context, and I06-I10
